audit.whatIsWrong: Chart rows 0, 3, 5 and 6 disagree with the mirror audit and, on rows 5 and 6, with their own whys[] text.
audit.why: The sett__tryndamere mirror set the chart to Tryndamere, Sett, Sett, Sett, Sett, Tryndamere, Tryndamere. whys[5] and whys[6] here already say 'favours Tryndamere' while the rows read Skill.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 5 and 6 to Tryndamere and row 3 to Sett, as matched full/content pairs with ratings and reasons.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere in the spike or cooldown text.
audit.why: Haymaker 18/16.5/15/13.5/12, Facebreaker 16/14.5/13/11.5/10, The Show Stopper 120/100/80, Undying Rage 120/100/80. Sett's lane spike is Grit storage from levels 2-5; yours is Stridebreaker into Infinity Edge, which is why 5 and 6 flip back.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[1].d and spikes[1].text.

audit.whatIsWrong: Knuckle Down is called a slow in three places. It is not a slow. Facebreaker is described as an unconditional grab-stun. spikes[1].text calls The Show Stopper a 'suppress-slam'.
audit.why: Riot's Knuckle Down text: next two attacks deal bonus max-health damage and Sett gains Move Speed while moving toward enemy champions — speed on his side, no slow on yours. Facebreaker 'pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him... If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned', so alone in lane you are slowed unless a minion sits on his far side. Haymaker also stores Grit from damage Sett takes, meaning your own trade loads his burst, and only its centre is true damage. Riot's Show Stopper text says carry-and-slam; suppression is not in this data.
audit.corrected: Knuckle Down restated as his move speed; Facebreaker's opposite-sides condition stated; Haymaker's centre-true-damage and self-loading Grit stated; the suppression claim dropped rather than asserted.

edits.before: Spin up fury on the wave before contesting anything. Identify how Sett contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Spin up fury on the wave — with no Grit stored, Haymaker is a weak punch and Knuckle Down is his only real level-1 threat.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Haymaker's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: His window: stored Grit makes Haymaker hurt and Knuckle Down's speed sticks him to you. Give ground, farm safe, wait for items.

edits.before: Stridebreaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Haymaker's cooldown.
edits.after: Stridebreaker plus crit lifesteal out-races Haymaker — force the fight the moment it completes.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Sett carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on: you outscale a tanky Sett 1v1 and split past his burst — close before the map decides instead of you.

edits.before: Level 1 is even skill — Sett hasn't stored grit yet, so early punches trade evenly with your crits.
edits.after: Level 1 favours Tryndamere — Sett has no Grit stored, so Haymaker is a weak punch and you win the walk-up.

edits.before: Level 4-5 favours Sett — stored Haymaker and Q slow let him win every extended exchange.
edits.after: Level 4-5 favours Sett — stored Grit and Knuckle Down's charge speed win him every extended exchange.

edits.before: Sett's window — with Haymaker (W) shield-into-true-damage stored from Pit Grit (passive) punches and Knuckle Down (Q) slow, he wins every extended trade and can chunk you hard before your crits scale.
edits.after: Sett's window — Grit stores from damage he takes, so your own crits load Haymaker (W), and only its centre is true damage. Knuckle Down (Q) is speed toward you, not a slow, and it wins him the extended trade.

edits.before: Sett still edges you: Facebreaker (E) grab plus The Show Stopper (R) suppress-slam is a real kill threat, and even with R Undying Rage he can trade you down and reset before your ult window ends.
edits.after: Sett still edges you: Facebreaker (E) only stuns when targets sit on both sides of him, so alone you are slowed — but with a minion behind you, E into The Show Stopper (R) is a real kill threat.

edits.before: Levels 2 through 5 belong to Sett: stored Haymaker true damage, Q slow, and at 6 the E-R combo give him kill pressure and win every extended trade before your crit scaling arrives.
edits.after: Levels 2 through 5 belong to Sett: stored Haymaker true damage and Knuckle Down's charge speed, then at 6 the E-R combo, give him kill pressure before your crit scaling arrives.

edits.before: Use Knuckle Down (Q) slow to stick and win extended early trades
edits.after: Use Knuckle Down (Q) speed to stick and win extended early trades

edits.before: - Sett Haymaker: matchup-defining — His shield + true-damage burst. Crit after it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Haymaker: 18s at rank 1, and your own damage fills the Grit — only its centre is true damage, so stand at the edge. - Facebreaker: 16s, and it stuns only from opposite sides. - Undying Rage: 120s at rank 1.

edits.before: Track Sett's Haymaker: His shield + true-damage burst. Crit after it. When it is down — Crit him down.
edits.after: Haymaker's centre is true damage — stand at its edge. Facebreaker only stuns you from opposite sides.

edits.before: His shield + true-damage burst. Crit after it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Grit comes from damage he takes — your crits load it. Bait Haymaker at 18s, then commit.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Facebreaker is 16s and stuns you when a minion sits on his far side.

notes: The packet suspectName 'Use Knuckle Down' is a FALSE POSITIVE on the name — but the line around it was wrong anyway: Knuckle Down has no slow. Left unverified: whether The Show Stopper applies suppression, and whether it can be cast on Tryndamere during Undying Rage. Riot's text says only carry-and-slam, so I removed the 'suppress-slam' claim rather than restating it.
